dependentDeduction.title: Dependent Deduction Checker
dependentDeduction.subtitle: {year} tax year · Enter each family member's birth year and income to see whether you can claim them, why, and how much tax you save
dependentDeduction.salaryHint: Annual pay minus non-taxable allowances such as meal pay. Used only to calculate the tax saved.

me.female: I am a woman (women's additional deduction, 500,000 KRW)
me.single: I have no spouse (single, divorced or widowed — single-parent deduction, 1,000,000 KRW)
me.hint: The women's deduction requires comprehensive income of 30M KRW or less (gross pay about 41.47M KRW); without a spouse you must be a household head with dependents. If both apply, only the single-parent deduction of 1,000,000 KRW is given.

family.title: Family
family.hint: Judged as of December 31, {year}. The age test is met if it applies on any day of the year. Enter income for all of {year}.

row.name: {rel} · born {born}
row.title: Member {n}
row.disabled: Has a disability (no age test, extra 2,000,000 KRW)
row.together: Registered at the same address (temporary absence for school or illness counts)
row.more: Other income (daily wages, business, private pension, financial, other) · {n} entered

relHint.spouse: No age test; only the income test applies.
relHint.parent: Your spouse's parents and grandparents count too. They may live apart for housing reasons if you actually support them.
relHint.child: May live apart. Must be 20 or younger unless disabled.
relHint.grandchild: A lineal descendant, so the same age test as children (20 or younger).
relHint.sibling: Your spouse's siblings count too. Must be registered at your address and share a household.
relHint.foster: A child in family foster care. Check the decree for details such as the care period.
relHint.recipient: A recipient under the National Basic Living Security Act who lives with you. No age test.

wage.label: Employment income (gross pay)
wage.hint: Salary or part-time pay, excluding non-taxable items. Up to 5,000,000 KRW is fine if this is the only income.

daily.label: Daily wages
daily.hint: Daily wages are taxed separately, so they never count.

business.label: Business income amount
business.hint: Revenue minus necessary expenses (the income amount on the tax return).

publicPension.label: Public pension total (National, civil service, military, private school)
publicPension.hint: Taxable pension (contributions from 2002 on, shown on the pension withholding receipt). With no other income, up to {limit} KRW a year is fine.

privatePension.label: Private pension (pension savings / IRP payouts)
privatePension.hint: Up to 15M KRW a year can be taxed separately, so we treat it as excluded.

financial.label: Interest and dividends
financial.hint: 20M KRW or less a year is taxed separately and excluded.

other.label: Other income amount (e.g. lecture fees minus expenses)
other.hint: 3M KRW or less can be taxed separately, so we treat it as excluded.

capitalGains.label: Capital gains amount (real estate, shares)
capitalGains.hint: Gain minus the long-term holding deduction. Zero if exempt as a one-home household.

retirement.label: Retirement income (severance received this year)
retirement.hint: The full taxable severance counts, so above 1,000,000 KRW they cannot be claimed that year.

age.parent: Must be born in {parent} or earlier (60 or older)
age.child: Must be born in {young} or later (20 or younger)
age.grandchild: Must be born in {young} or later (20 or younger)
age.foster: Must be born in {young} or later (20 or younger)
age.sibling: Must be born in {young} or later (20 or younger) or in {parent} or earlier (60 or older)

fail.apart: Siblings and recipients must be registered at your address and share a household
fail.wage: Even with employment income only, gross pay of {wage} KRW is over 5,000,000 KRW
fail.income: Income amount is over 1,000,000 KRW because of {sources} (total {total} KRW)

dependentDeduction.ok: Meets both the age and income tests

note.noAge: No age test because of the disability
note.pensionLimit: With public pension only, up to {limit} KRW passes
note.elderlyLost: Being 70 or older, they would also have added the 1,000,000 KRW senior deduction

result.label: Tax saved thanks to your family (incl. local tax)
result.sub: {n} of {total} eligible · basic {basic} KRW + additional {extra} KRW
result.dualNote: Dual income: combined saving for both of you under the current split.

self.single: Your single-parent deduction {amount} KRW (no spouse, with an eligible child)

dependentDeduction.reform: The government's August 2026 tax reform proposal would raise the income limit to 3M KRW and the employment-only gross pay limit to 7.5M KRW. It is still before the National Assembly with no confirmed start year, so it is not in the calculation. We will update it if passed.

share.label: Gross pay {salaryM}M KRW · {n} of {total} family members claimed
share.headline: Tax down {saving} KRW
share.text: With gross pay of {salaryM}M KRW, {n} of {total} family members qualify as dependents and tax falls by {saving} KRW.

couple.title: Dual income: who should claim
couple.desc: Each parent or child can be claimed by only one spouse. We try every split to find the one with the lowest combined tax.
couple.spouseSalaryHint: Once entered, you can pick who currently claims each family member.
couple.empty: Enter your spouse's gross pay to compare.
couple.best: A different split saves {gain} KRW more
couple.same: Your current split is already the best
couple.note: Tax saved, including local tax. An approximation from gross pay alone, assuming no other deductions. The women's and single-parent deductions do not depend on the split, so they are left out.
couple.capped: With many family members, only the first {n} are moved; the rest stay as they are now.
couple.warning: Two people must not claim the same family member. If siblings each claim the same parent, one claim is later cancelled and the underpaid tax plus a penalty is due. Agree on who claims before year-end settlement.

age.sibling: Born {young} or later, or {parent} or earlier
age.foster: Treated as born {young} or later (details in the decree)

rules.ageNote: The age test is met if it applies on any day of the year (Income Tax Act Art. 53). No age test for people with disabilities; those born in {elderly} or earlier (70+) add a 1,000,000 KRW senior deduction.
rules.incomeTitle: Income test: annual income amount of 1,000,000 KRW or less
income: Income amount is comprehensive income (employment, business, pension, interest, dividends, other) plus retirement and capital gains. Non-taxable and separately taxed income is excluded.
With employment income only, gross pay up to 5,000,000 KRW is fine. Combined with other income, the employment income amount (gross pay minus the employment income deduction) is added.
Public pensions count after the pension income deduction, so with no other income up to {limit} KRW a year passes.
Interest and dividends up to 20M KRW, daily wages, private pensions up to 15M KRW (separate taxation chosen) and other income up to 3M KRW (separate taxation chosen) are excluded.
A one-time severance payment or a real estate or share gain easily pushes income over 1,000,000 KRW. Only that year is affected; the next year is judged again.

compare.title: Not the same as health insurance dependents
compare.desc: The year-end dependent deduction follows the Income Tax Act (1,000,000 KRW income amount, age tests). Health insurance dependents follow the National Health Insurance Act (20M KRW income and property tests). Someone can be a health insurance dependent but not a tax dependent, and vice versa.
compare.linkDesc: Check the 20M KRW income and property tests

dependentDeduction.source: Basis: Income Tax Act Arts. 50, 51, 53, 47-2, 14(3), 59-2 · {year} tax year (laws in force as of November 2026)
